title: 13 Best Herbal Creams For Painful Swallowing
intro: Herbal creams for painful swallowing are topical preparations that contain natural extracts from plants and herbs, used to alleviate discomfort and inflammation in the throat and esophagus. These creams have numerous benefits, including promoting relaxation, reducing pain and inflammation, and soothing irritated tissues. Examples of herbal creams used to treat painful swallowing include Aloe vera gel, which provides anti-inflammatory properties, Echinacea cream, which boosts the immune system, and Slippery elm cream, which soothes and protects the mucous membranes. Additionally, other herbal creams such as Licorice root, Marshmallow root, and Myrrh are also used to treat this ailment, as they possess anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties that help to calm the throat and reduce discomfort.

preparations.preparation_desc: Zingiber officinale creams, derived from the rhizome of the ginger plant, have been traditionally used to treat the painful swallowing ailment known as dysphagia. These creams possess anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, which help to reduce pain and inflammation in the throat, thereby making swallowing easier and more comfortable. The bioactive constituents of Zingiber officinale, including gingerols and shogaols, have been found to have potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which contribute to its therapeutic benefits in treating dysphagia. The use of Zingiber officinale creams to treat dysphagia offers several benefits, including relief from pain and discomfort, improved swallowing function, and enhanced overall quality of life.

The benefits of using Glycyrrhiza glabra creams to treat esophagitis include rapid relief from pain and inflammation, promotion of healing, and prevention of further irritation and complications.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand = Chotmaihet thangphaet", Glycyrrhiza glabra creams may offer some relief for painful swallowing due to their antimicrobial activity, particularly against S. pyogenes ATCC 19615, with MIC and MBC values at 39 and 78 μg/ml, respectively.
